Vary brightness, contrast, saturation and hue of training images.

Each training image gets its own factors, applied in a random order (torchvision ColorJitter): brightness, contrast and saturation factors from [max(0, 1 - v), 1 + v], a hue shift from [-hue, hue]. 0 turns an adjustment off. Saturation and hue leave one-channel images unchanged. Validation and test images pass through unchanged.

## Settings

| Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brightness | `brightness` | Number | `0.2` | `>=0` | The run | Brightness spread, 0 or more. |
| Contrast | `contrast` | Number | `0.2` | `>=0` | The run | Contrast spread, 0 or more. |
| Saturation | `saturation` | Number | `0.2` | `>=0` | The run | Saturation spread, 0 or more. |
| Hue | `hue` | Number | `0.1` | `0-0.5` | The run | Hue shift, 0 to 0.5. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Where it runs

| Where | Runs |
| --- | --- |
| Data pipeline (run the graph, **Run step**, previews) | No: Color Jitter is a training image transform: the image batcher runs it on the ArrayFire device between Resize and Normalize; PipelineExecutor image transforms are not implemented |
| Training (the compiled model) | Yes, as a preprocessing step |

The node runs on the device chosen for the run (CPU or a GPU); a node does not fix a device.

## Usage

```text
Resize -> Color Jitter -> Normalize -> Conv2D
```

```text
Each image gets its own factors, applied in a random order: brightness, contrast and saturation from [max(0, 1 - v), 1 + v], hue shifted by [-hue, hue]. Validation and test pass through.
```

## Tips

- Helps models that must cope with different lighting and cameras.
